title: Regularity of purely inseparable base changes of the characteristic-p generic formal fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $n,m\ge0$ and $A=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] in $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over the formal power series ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; it is a Noetherian domain. Let $K=\kappa((0))=A_{(0)}$ be its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal and $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge=\varprojlim_rA_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^rA_{\mathfrak p}$ the completion of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ at its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].. For every finite purely inseparable extension L/K, L tensor_K ((A_q)^completion tensor_A K) is a regular ring. Noetherianity of the original fibre is not part of this statement.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR, induction and derivation argument

proof.text: (Base case.) The ring $A=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ is regular: $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], the polynomial extension is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], and regularity ascends along this smooth map by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent]. Thus $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], its completion is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], and every localization of that completion, in particular $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_AK$, is regular. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and localization of a Noetherian ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, base case $L=K$; Lemma Tag 07NY (completion-regular)

proof.text: (Induction setup.) For a finite purely inseparable extension $L/K$, let $P(L)$ be the assertion that $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_A L$ is Noetherian and regular. We prove $P(L)$ by induction on $[L:K]$. The degree-one case is Step 1. If $[L:K]>1$, apply the public degree-$p$ tower node [lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-degree-p-intermediate] to obtain an intermediate field $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$ and $z\in L$ with $L=M(z)$, $z^p=f\in M$, $[L:M]=p$, and $[M:K]<[L:K]$; hence $P(M)$ is the induction hypothesis. Since $[L:M]=p$, $f$ is not a $p$th power in $M$, or else $z\in M$ and the degree would be one. Steps 3 and 4 transport $P(M)$ to $P(L)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR, proof, induction on $[L:K]$ and the degree-$p$ intermediate field

proof.text: (Finite model, the substitution $z\mapsto sz$, primes, and the 07N9 identifications.) By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-subalgebra-fraction-field] choose a subring $B\subseteq M$ containing $A$, finite as an $A$-module, with fraction field $M$; it is a domain with $p=0$, being a subring of the field $M$. (Substitution.) As $f\in M=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, write $f=b/s$ with $b,s\in B$, $s\neq0$. Put $z'=sz\in L$ and $f'=s^pf=s^{p-1}b\in B$. Then $z'^p=s^pz^p=s^pf=f'$; $M(z')=M(z)=L$ since $s\in M^\times$; $[L:M]=p$ is unchanged; and $f'$ is not a $p$th power in $M$, because $f'=u^p$ with $u\in M$ would give $f=(u/s)^p$, while $f$ is not a $p$th power (Step 2) and $s^p$ is one. Replacing $z,f$ by $z',f'$ we assume from now on: $f\in B$, $L=M(z)$, $z^p=f$, $[L:M]=p$, and $f$ is not a $p$th power in $M$. (The ring $C$.) $A$ is regular (Step 1), hence Noetherian, so $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. Put $C=B[z]/(z^p-f)$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Division by the monic polynomial $z^p-f$ shows that $C$ is a free $B$-module with basis $1,z,\ldots,z^{p-1}$; so $C$ is finite over $B$, and finite over $A$ (the products of $A$-module generators of $B$ with $1,\ldots,z^{p-1}$ generate). The $B$-algebra map $C\to L$, $z\mapsto z$, is injective: an element $\sum_{i<p}b_iz^i$ of its kernel is a polynomial relation of degree $<p$ for $z$ over $M$, and the minimal polynomial of $z$ over $M$ has degree $[L:M]=p$, so all $b_i=0$. Its image contains $B$ and $z$, so its fraction field contains $M(z)=L$. Hence $C$ is a domain with fraction field $L$. Likewise $C\otimes_BM=M[z]/(z^p-f)\to L$ is surjective ($L=M[z]$) between $M$-vector spaces of dimension $p$, hence $C\otimes_BM\cong L$ as $C$-algebras. (Primes.) Every localization of the regular ring $A$ at a prime is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal], so the domain $A$ is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal]. $A\subseteq B$ is a finite extension of domains whose fraction field extension $M/K$ is finite purely inseparable (a subextension of $L/K$), so [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-integral-prime-unique] gives exactly one prime $\mathfrak r\subset B$ with $\mathfrak r\cap A=\mathfrak p$. The ring $B$ need not be normal, and none is needed: [lem-weil-pbc-radicial-prime-unique-degree-p] applies to the domain $B$ with $p=0$, the element $f\in B$ and the domain $C=B[z]/(z^p-f)$, and gives that $c^p\in B$ for every $c\in C$ and that exactly one prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ has $\mathfrak q\cap B=\mathfrak r$. A prime of $C$ over $\mathfrak p$ contracts to a prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, which is $\mathfrak r$; so $\mathfrak q$ is the only prime of $C$ over $\mathfrak p$. (The local ring $C_{\mathfrak q}$.) Let $C'=C\otimes_BB_{\mathfrak r}=B_{\mathfrak r}[z]/(z^p-f)$, the localization of $C$ at the image of $B\setminus\mathfrak r$. Its primes are $\mathfrak q'C'$ for primes $\mathfrak q'\subset C$ with $\mathfrak q'\cap B\subseteq\mathfrak r$; for such $\mathfrak q'$ and $c\in\mathfrak q'$ we have $c^p\in\mathfrak q'\cap B\subseteq\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so $c\in\mathfrak q$. Thus every prime of $C'$ lies in the prime $\mathfrak qC'$: $C'$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qC'$ over $\mathfrak rB_{\mathfrak r}$, the elements of $C\setminus\mathfrak q$ are units of $C'$, and $C'=C_{\mathfrak q}$. $B_{\mathfrak r}$ is a Noetherian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], so [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-quotient] gives $(C_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\cong(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge[z]/(z^p-f)=(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge\otimes_BC$ compatibly with the maps from $B_{\mathfrak r}[z]$, hence as $C$-algebras. (Identifications.) Apply Algebra Lemma 07N9 [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] to the Noetherian ring $A$, the finite $A$-algebra $B$ and $\mathfrak p$ (one prime $\mathfrak r$ over it): $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_AB\cong(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge$ as $B$-algebras; applying $-\otimes_BM$ and $(X\otimes_AB)\otimes_BM=X\otimes_AM$ gives (*) $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_AM\cong R:=(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge\otimes_BM$ as $M$-algebras. Apply 07N9 to $A$, the finite $A$-algebra $C$ and $\mathfrak p$ (one prime $\mathfrak q$ over it): $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_AC\cong(C_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\cong(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge\otimes_BC$ as $C$-algebras. Applying $-\otimes_CL$ with $L=C\otimes_BM$ gives (**) $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_AL\cong(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge\otimes_BC\otimes_BM=R\otimes_BB[z]/(z^p-f)=R[z]/(z^p-f)$ as $L$-algebras.

A_p^ (x)_A M = B_r^ (x)_B M ... the completion of C = B[z]/(z^p-f) equals B_r^[z]/(z^p-f)'; Algebra, Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension); Algebra, Lemma Tag 030B (lemma-normality-is-local)

proof.text: (Derivation extension and the degree-$p$ quotient.) The domain $B$ of Step 3 has $p=0$ and is of finite type over the Noetherian $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$-adically complete local ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ ([lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] (1), (3)): it is generated as a $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$-algebra by $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ and finitely many $A$-module generators of $B$. Since $f\in B$ is not a $p$th power in $M$ (Step 3), [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-nonzero-on-non-pth-power] supplies a derivation $D:B\to B$ with $D(f)\ne0$. First extend $D$ from $B$ to $B_{\mathfrak r}$ by the quotient formula $D(a/s)=D(a)/s-aD(s)/s^2$ ([lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends] (2)); then extend it to $(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge$ by the compatible maps $D_n:B_{\mathfrak r}/(\mathfrak rB_{\mathfrak r})^{n+1}\to B_{\mathfrak r}/(\mathfrak rB_{\mathfrak r})^n$ ([lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends] (1)); finally extend it to $R=(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge\otimes_BM$, the localization of $(B_{\mathfrak r})^\wedge$ at the image of $B\setminus\{0\}$, by the same localization formula. These extensions agree with $D$ on $B$, so they send $f$ to the image of $D(f)$, which is a nonzero element of $M$ and therefore a unit in the $M$-algebra $R$. By $P(M)$ and the identification (*) of Step 3, $R$ is Noetherian and regular. The polynomial-smooth node [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] makes $R\to R[z]$ smooth, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] therefore makes the polynomial ring $R[z]$ regular. Extend the derivation on $R$ to $\overline D:R[z]\to R[z]$ by $\overline D(z)=0$, i.e. $\overline D(\sum r_iz^i)=\sum D(r_i)z^i$. Then $\overline D(z^p-f)=-D(f)$, whose image in $R[z]/(z^p-f)$ is a unit. Apply the hypersurface node [lem-weil-pbc-hypersurface-derivation-regular] to the regular ring $R[z]$, the element $z^p-f$, and $\overline D$: the ring $R[z]/(z^p-f)$ is regular, in particular Noetherian. By the identification (**) of Step 3 it is isomorphic to $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_AL$, which proves $P(L)$.

theorem formalFiber_polynomial_geometricComponent
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (n m : ℕ)
    (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))) [q.IsPrime] :
    let A := MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)
    let C := AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
      (Localization.AtPrime q)
    ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k']
      [Module.Finite ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k']
      [IsPurelyInseparable ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k'],
      IsRegularRing (TensorProduct ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k'
        ((⊥ : Ideal A).Fiber C))
